issues.title: Saab 291-2494 requires boost-control fault isolation before condemning a turbo
issues.cause: November 2004 all-market factory bulletin documents many misdiagnosed turbo returns and directs diaphragm, wastegate, hose, vacuum and compressor condition checks.
symptoms: whistling or smoke can have several causes
issues.diagnosis_summary: Capture ECU/hardware/software identification, codes, then independently verify bypass seal, wastegate actuation, relevant vacuum circuit and charge-air hose leaks; evaluate actual shaft/wheel damage only using corrected factory source and exact turbo specification.
issues.correction_summary: Repair confirmed boost control, leaks or actuator separately. Order mechanical turbo only after evidence of internal damage and verified current OE configuration.
limits: All markets bulletin 291-2494 (November 2004) is NOT the restricted non-US/CA B205E/B235E E-clip bulletin 291-2317 (January 2002).
Shaft play line 'axial up/down' is internally inconsistent; 1–2mm MUST NOT be used as an acceptance criterion.
The WIS /1998/ mirror path is not the November 2004 bulletin effective date.

issues.title: MY2005/2009 TCM adaptation is a service consequence, not a generic harsh-shift cure
issues.cause: Factory adaptation procedure follows automatic transmission, TCM or software service; TCM uses durable learning that may mask wear and survive battery disconnect.
symptoms: rough gear engagement after gearbox, TCM or software replacement
seller claims gearbox fixed by unplugging battery
issues.diagnosis_summary: Compare original gearbox/engine TCM programming, repairs, actual ATF temperature and codes. Reproduce only in controlled, safe, roadworthy circumstances.
issues.correction_summary: After correctly matched repairs, qualified technician performs full Tech 2 adaptation. Do not indiscriminately reset or use stall testing to warm unit.
limits: Not proof that an adaptation reset cures physical clutch/valve-body damage.
Factory explicitly forbids warming transmission with a stall test.
Availability of modern Tech 2/SPS security and software has not been established.

issues.title: 2005 input-speed sensor code versus 2009 5th-gear ratio error
issues.cause: P0717 in MY2005 relates to lost input sensor with output-speed fallback, while MY2009 P0735 means a calculated 5th-gear ratio diverges beyond 20%.
issues.diagnosis_summary: Check actual year-specific code and criteria plus TCM live input/output data, selector/ATF status, harness and vehicle-specific failure symptoms; avoid conflating missing signal with positive ratio mismatch.
issues.correction_summary: Repair confirmed sensor/harness error when established. If true ratio slip persists, evaluate transmission internals and cost before purchase.
limits: P0735 is not a confirmed worn clutch without further diagnosis.
P0717 is not guaranteed to be only a cheap electrical fix.
2005 and 2009 diagnostic source year differences are preserved.
